critique.evidence: The headline promises “One payment. Two very different answers,” but the selected trace shows Legacy ALLOW and Intent Integrity ALLOW, so the central claim is not demonstrated. The copy also says no intent playback and no structured cart were recorded, then claims the decision came from comparing the paid cart with the delegated mission. “Select any cached transaction” is understandable, but the rows do not look strongly actionable and “Inspect the causal seam” has weak affordance. On desktop, the fixed navigation obscures part of the oversized headline; mobile is legible but requires a long scroll before reaching the comparison.
critique.fix: Default to a trace with a visible decision split, such as Legacy ALLOW versus Intent Integrity BLOCK, and show the exact evidence causing that divergence. Remove the contradictory cart/intent language, style rows and “Inspect the causal seam” as obvious controls, and prevent the desktop header from overlapping the headline.
